### J-1 The tasks skill still waits for the spec jury on a bug fix
- quote: "Use after the plan jury approves (or, for a bug fix, after the spec jury does)"
- quote: "the slug of a spec whose spec jury approved it, or which the human closed with a reason"
- quote: "the tasks skill's step 4 stops on an `escalate:` note"
- quote: "on `route: lite`, `may_start` returns `(True, ...)` when `spec.check(root, slug, gate=True)` has no errors"
- situation (architecture-fit): CT-3 lets `nio new tasks` start a lite effort once the grill passes, with no spec jury. CT-7 changes only step 4 of `skills/tasks/SKILL.md`. Its description, its Inputs, and step 1 ("It refuses ... when the spec isn't approved") still tell the agent that a bug fix needs an approved spec jury first. An agent following the skill text would stop, or send the effort to a spec jury that the lite route skips.
- fix: widen CT-7, or add a contract on `skills/tasks/SKILL.md`, so the description, Inputs and step 1 say a lite spec starts once `nio check spec --gate` passes.
- validation: confirmed: CT-7 edits only step 4 of `skills/tasks/SKILL.md`, while its description (line 3, "for a bug fix, after the spec jury does"), Input (line 18, "spec jury approved it") and step 1 (line 43, "isn't approved") still require the spec jury that CT-3 and FR-2 skip on lite; no other contract binds those lines.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-7: tasks skill description, Inputs and step 1 start a bug fix on nio check spec --gate

### J-2 `Mode: direct` is put on the drafter, but the evaluator sets `Mode:`
- quote: "`Mode: direct` as the drafter proposes it"
- quote: "It sets every `Tier:` (with a reason), `Mode:` and `Effort:`"
- quote: "Leave `Tier:` and `Effort:` as `strong: to be rated` and `med`: the evaluator rates them."
- situation (architecture-fit): In the existing flow the drafter card never writes `Mode:`, and tasks-skill step 3 has the evaluator set every `Mode:`, with "rating lines" as the only lines it may change. CT-8 only edits the drafter card. The evaluator can still rate the unchanged-behaviour task `split` or `single`, which drops FR-7's `direct` guarantee. No contract binds the evaluator card or step 3.
- fix: add the rule to the evaluator's card or tasks-skill step 3 (a bug fix's unchanged-behaviour task keeps `Mode: direct`), or have `nio check tasks` enforce it on a lite spec.
- validation: confirmed: `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` line 50 has the evaluator set every `Mode:` after the drafter, and CT-8 edits only the drafter card; nothing binds the evaluator or `nio check tasks` to keep `direct` on the unchanged-behaviour task, so FR-7's guarantee can be overwritten.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-14: evaluator card keeps a preservation task Mode: direct; tasks step 3 says it

### J-3 A skipped stage gets two different labels
- quote: "`skipped: lite route` for a route's own; `done` prints `skipped <stage> (not built)` or `skipped <stage> (lite route)`; `next` prints `skipped: <stages> (not built)` as today, with the route's stages among them"
- situation (architecture-fit): The same skip of spec_jury, planning or plan_jury appears as "lite route" in history and in `done`'s output. `nio flow next` calls it "(not built)", although those stages are built. The existing `next_step` line `skipped: {...} (not built)` was written only for `NOT_BUILT` stages.
- fix: have `next` give each skipped stage its own label, the same way `done` does.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-1: next prints not-built and lite-route skips on separate lines

- quote: "If it prints neither (a lite or bug-fix spec, or no `nio`), say the next stage is the implement stage."
- quote: "If it prints neither (a lite or bug-fix spec, or no `nio`), say the next stage is the grill."

### J-5 A declined escalation re-stops the lite effort on every run
- quote: "the tasks skill stops on it"
- quote: "stops on an `escalate:` note"
- quote: "continue the effort on lite and log the human's call"
- situation (logic): A lite spec has two non-test folders, `src/a/x.py` and `src/b/y.py`. `nio check tasks` prints `escalate:`, the tasks skill stops and offers the full flow, and the human declines. CT-13 logs `## Call · escalation declined` in `grill.md`, and the effort goes on. `check` still prints the note on every later run, because CT-4 only says "Errors and exit code are unchanged by it". That covers the tasking guard, the tasks jury plan and any re-run after a tasks-jury rejection. CT-7 says the skill stops on the note, and nothing in CT-4 or CT-7 reads the logged decline. So FR-11 (the effort continues on lite) and CT-7 (stop on the note) give two outcomes for the same state.
- fix: say in CT-7 that the stop is skipped when `grill.md` already holds an escalation-declined call naming that trigger. Or have CT-4 leave the note out once the call is logged.
- validation: confirmed: CT-4 leaves the `escalate:` note on every `check` run ("Errors and exit code are unchanged"), CT-7 says the skill stops on the note, and CT-13 only logs the decline in `grill.md`; nothing in CT-4 or CT-7 reads that log, so a declined effort re-stops on the next run, against FR-11.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-7: step 4 skips the stop when grill.md logs a declined call for that trigger

### J-6 The folder trigger can't fire for a fix task appended after the tasks check
- quote: "IF a lite fix changes non-test files in more than one folder"
- quote: "when the non-test files named by every task's `Files:` line (`files` then `file_of`) have more than one direct parent folder"
- situation (logic): The tasks gate passes with all files in `src/a`. The implementation jury then rejects the fix, and the existing loop appends a fix task under `#### Fixes` whose `Files:` names `src/b/z.py`. In `guard`, the implementing stage runs `implement.left`, not `tasks.check`, so no `escalate:` note appears and the effort goes on in two folders. FR-8 says the trigger covers the fix as changed. CT-4 only evaluates the planned `Files:` lines when `check` happens to run. CT-12 covers only a blocked handoff that names a dependency, an interface or stored data. A second folder is not in its list.
- fix: add the folder trigger to CT-12's list, or say in CT-4 that the count is re-run when a fix task is appended.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-12: a fix task in a second folder offers the full flow

### J-7 Escalation window differs between AC-11 and the state table
- quote: "Given a lite effort at tasking or later"
- quote: "| drafting | → grilling | ignore | → full route | [agent] |"
- situation (logic): The table moves drafting and grilling to "full route" on a rewrite. CT-6 has the grill stop and offer the full flow, which is escalation at grilling. AC-11 and its TC-11 only cover a lite effort "at tasking or later". An escalation accepted at grilling has no AC or test for where the effort stands. FR-10 puts no stage limit on the switch.
- fix: drop "at tasking or later" from AC-11, or cover the drafting and grilling rows with their own observable.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-11 adds an escalation from grilling

### J-8 TC-1 never calls the lite gate of `may_start`, so `nio new tasks` can stay broken on a lite effort
- quote: "then `tasks.md` written from `tests/fixtures/tasks/tasks.md` cut to the bug fix's ACs (AC-1, AC-2) so `nio check tasks` passes"
- quote: "on `route: lite`, `may_start` returns `(True, ...)` when `spec.check(root, slug, gate=True)` has no errors"
- quote: "if jury.standing(root, slug, "spec") not in ("approved", "closed"):"
- quote: "Use from @nio:tasks after `nio new tasks`."
- situation (test-proof): `may_start` is called only from `tasks.new`. TC-1 writes `tasks.md` from a fixture and never calls `tasks.new`. If CT-3 is left undone, `may_start` still returns "the spec must be approved first" on a lite effort, because a lite effort has no spec jury, so the real lite path breaks at `nio new tasks`. TC-1 still passes.
- fix: in TC-1, create `tasks.md` through `tasks.new(root, S)` (or assert `tasks.may_start(root, S)[0]` is True) after `done grilling`. Also add an assert that it returns False with the stated message when the gate check fails.
- validation: confirmed: `may_start` in `src/nio/tasks.py` is called only from `tasks.new`, and still requires `jury.standing(root, slug, "spec")` approved or closed (line 41), which a lite effort never has; TC-1 writes `tasks.md` from a fixture and never calls `tasks.new` or `may_start`, so it passes with CT-3 undone.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-1 creates tasks.md through tasks.new and asserts may_start's refusal before the grill

### J-9 TC-5's refusal comes from the undone task, not the epic gate, and done is never reached
- quote: "one commit `T-1: fix` touching a file."
- quote: "`done implementing` exits 1 with an output naming a task not done or the epic's missing `epic` line, and history gains no `implementing → done` line."
- quote: "each task not done with what it still needs, then each"
- quote: "Observable: `nio jury plan <slug> implementation-E-1` on a lite effort plans the conformance and correctness lenses, and `nio flow next` reaches done only after the epic's gate passes."
- situation (test-proof): in the setup, T-1 has a commit but no red or green lines, so `implement.left` already lists "T-1 is ...: needs ..." and `done implementing` exits 1 whatever the epic gate does. If a lite bug skips or auto-closes the implementation gate, TC-5 still passes, because the assert accepts either reason. No test drives a lite effort to `done` after an approval, so a lite effort that can never reach done also passes (TC-1 stops at implementing).
- fix: bring T-1 to done first. Then assert that `done implementing` names "E-1 has no epic line" (or that `next` shows `implementation-E-1 is open`). After approving the gate with `flow.done(root, "implementation-E-1", S, by=BY)`, assert that history gains `implementing → done`.
- validation: confirmed: TC-5's setup gives T-1 only a commit, so `implement.left` (line 691) already reports "T-1 is ...: needs ..." and `done implementing` exits 1 regardless of the epic gate; the assert accepts either reason, and no test reaches `implementing → done` on a lite effort.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-5 brings E-1's tasks to done, asserts the missing epic line, then done after the gate
